An Ordinance to amend the Town of Pine Mountain Ordinance to Regulate and Tax Alcohol; to provide an effective date to repeal all ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith; and for other purposes.

WHEREAS, the Town of Pine Mountain adopted a comprehensive ordinance to regulate and tax alcohol, which was signed into law on October 12, 2020 (the “Alcohol Ordinance”); and

WHEREAS, House Bill 879, signed into law by Governor Kemp on August 3, 2020, states that an authorized package retailer with an on-premise pour license may provide for the home delivery of malt beverages and wine unless prohibited by municipal resolution or ordinance; and

WHEREAS, House Bill 879 further states that an authorized package retailer licensed to sell alcoholic beverages in unbroken packages for consumption off the premises, which is also a licensed retail package liquor store, may provide for the home delivery of malt beverages, wine, and/or distilled spirits unless prohibited by municipal resolution or ordinance upon the effective date of House Bill 879; and

WHEREAS, the Town of Pine Mountain desires to amend the Alcohol Ordinance to expressly prohibit the home delivery of malt beverages, wine, and/or distilled spirits within the limits of the Town of Pine Mountain as provided for in House Bill 879.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN, HARRIS COUNTY, GEORGIA, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE SAME, IT IS HEREBY ORDAINED AS FOLLOWS:
1:
That Section 1 of the Alcohol Ordinance is hereby amended to add the following subsection:

- (cc) Packaged goods retailer shall have the same meaning as provided in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-10.
2:
That Section 4 of the Alcohol Ordinance is hereby amended to add the following subsection:

- (c) Home Delivery of Alcohol. Pursuant to O.C.G.A. §-3-10(b), the Town of Pine Mountain hereby prohibits the delivery of any alcoholic beverages by any packaged goods retailer or licensed retail package liquor store located within the municipal boundaries of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, provided however that in-room service authorized by Section 6(d) shall not be prohibited.

Section Three.

All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby expressly repealed.

Section Four.

This amendment shall become effective on November 9 , 2020.
